newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares still in correction mood.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares still in correction mood.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell back on Thursday in moderat trade due to a new dealing system, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index lost 0.43 points to close at 234.49 points on turnover of 72.08 million pounds ($21.2 million).
"The new dealing system is still difficult for brokers to operate," said Mostafa Saad of Okaz Financial Brokerage. "The number of transactions is almost halved by the new system."

The volume was pushed up by the registration of 10 percent of East Delta Flour Mills, sold to employees as part of the privatisation programme. The 600,000 shares went through at the IPO price of 31.00 pounds.
"It was the millers' day with the biggest volume and highest increases," Saad told Reuters.
The market favourites Central and West Delta Flour Mills added 3.50 to finish at 54.00 pounds and Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 0.80 to close at 48.5.
"There are signs that the market would resume its upswin next week after this week's correction," Saad said.
Arab Cotton Ginning, majority privatised in mid-September, continued its strong performance on the exchange jumping 3.00 pounds to 35.00 pounds. More than 117,900 shares changed hands.
The CMA index for openly traded firms was down at 362.19 from 364.37 points on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 162.34 points from 162.23.
